insight.title: Coffee Lids Have a Tiny Second Hole to Save Your Face
insight.subtitle: Without this microscopic design feature, your morning brew would violently splash with every sip.
insight.notificationHook: Why coffee lids need a second hole

sections.text: Look closely at your disposable coffee lid. Opposite the drinking spout sits a microscopic pinhole. It seems useless—even counterintuitive for a lid meant to prevent spills. But it is entirely intentional.
Without that tiny hole, pouring liquid out creates a vacuum inside the cup. Air fights to get in through the drinking spout, causing the hot coffee to glug, splash, and scald your face.

The pinhole lets air enter the cup as coffee leaves. This neutralizes the pressure, allowing a smooth, continuous stream of caffeine to flow safely onto your tongue instead of exploding onto your shirt.
One microscopic hole keeps your morning commute stain-free.
